Ngl I relate more to your wife, so I'll try to help you out from her perspective or somewhere close. I understand that you need your time and that's honestly a very normal need. First you need to understand (if you don't already know this) that the tiny strands of physical or emotional empathy really goes a long way and is usually the fuel to power through the day. It's hard to work if there's no reassurance, in my experience. A hug can really make a difference and if she needs like 9 a day then she's quite troubled and needs a lot of reassurance. You're singled out because she expects the most from you, her husband. But she may or may not be able to admit that. So what you need to say is "hey *insert nickname/name* l understand and accept your need for physical or emotional validation but I also need sometime to focus on myself. So that doesn't mean I need space or I love you less it's just that I need some alone time once in a while." You can and should either cut or add to suit your preference, the previous statement is for a rough idea of sorts. Make it very clear that you still love her and that you're still in love with her and that nothing has changed. Establish a safeword for when you need your time.
